entities.name: The Wolf and the Seven Young Goats
entities.label: Text
entities.summary:
“The Wolf and the Seven Young Goats” is a European fairy tale collected by the Brothers Grimm (KHM 5) in which a wolf deceives and swallows six of seven kids while their mother is away; the youngest hides, the mother rescues the living children from the wolf’s belly, and the wolf is punished with stones. It encodes cautionary themes of stranger danger, obedience, and maternal protection.

As part of the Kinder- und Hausmärchen project, the tale entered the global children’s canon through translation and illustration, often softened or dramatised for pedagogy. Folklorists class it among ATAT beast tales of the devouring animal and miraculous rescue.

It remains one of the Grimms’ most familiar short narratives in childhood reading cultures worldwide.
